prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1241; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection with a vehicle that struck the claimant's car as it crossed oncoming traffic. Claimant states a wrist fracture resulted and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the claimant is a named driver on the policy in force at the time of loss. Coverage questions are being checked against the file.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene. Officers recorded the same sequence of movements the claimant described.

Entry 4: Statements from two independent witnesses match the claimant's account of the turn and the impact. Scene photos were received and reviewed.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage, which is consistent with the side and angle of impact described in the report. No earlier damage to the vehicle has been identified in prior records.

Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account of the collision in each call and in the written statement. Asked about any prior injury to the wrist and no earlier problems to that area are on record.

Entry 7: A neighbor contacted the office and believes the car showed body damage several weeks before the claimed loss date. This has not been verified and is being followed up.

Entry 8: Medical records show treatment for the wrist ran somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. It is not yet clear whether all of the treatment is related to this crash, and the medical file is under review.

Entry 9: File remains open pending the neighbor follow-up and medical review. Next step is to request the full treatment records and confirm the timeline of the reported damage.
